items.title: Data pipeline reliability toolkit
items.summary: Package retry-with-backoff, idempotency-key discipline, and schema-drift contract checks into one reusable reliability layer for data pipelines.
items.rationale: All three solve the same underlying problem -- failures and drift in long-running pipelines -- from different angles.

items.title: Bioinformatics plotting library with sane defaults
items.summary: A small plotting package baking in the Manhattan-plot layout and a color-blind-safe palette as defaults.
items.rationale: Both are visualization decisions that get re-solved from scratch on nearly every project that needs them.

items.title: "Don't ship this mistake" pre-launch checklist product
items.summary: A short, paid pre-launch checklist (client-side-only validation, SQL injection in admin tools, test-set leakage) for small teams without a dedicated reviewer.
items.rationale: Speculative -- these precautions are real and recurring, but unclear anyone would pay for a checklist rather than writing one themselves.

items.title: Backend reliability lint rules
items.summary: Static-analysis rules catching N+1 query loops, unbounded connection pools, and health checks that depend on the thing they check -- before code review has to.
items.rationale: All three are backend reliability mistakes with a recognizable code shape, which is exactly what a lint rule is good at catching.

items.title: Mobile offline-resilience starter kit
items.summary: A starter module combining on-device response caching, battery-aware polling, and offline-first state handling for mobile apps.
items.rationale: These three consistently show up together on mobile projects and are each easy to under-build in isolation.

items.title: Performance-tail dashboard product
items.summary: A hosted dashboard surfacing P99/GC-pause tail latency and profiler hotspots side by side, instead of the average-latency view most APM tools lead with.
items.rationale: Both ideas point at the same blind spot -- tools that show averages hide exactly the tail behavior that actually hurts users.
